newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain may take steps against Iberia, Spanair, AirEsp.
newsitem.headline: Spain may take steps against Iberia, Spanair, AirEsp.

text.p: Spain's competition commission said on Monday that it may take action against Iberia, Spanair and Air Espana for being anti-competitive.

"The competition service believes the companies could have taken advantage of an agreement to simultaneously increase and homogenise tariffs, which is an abuse of their collective position," the Economy Ministry said in a statement.
The commission said it started sanctions proceedings against the airlines. The three have time to defend themselves before the commission decides what measures to take.
The airlines announced last week that they would raise tariffs on national routes between 10 and 30 percent.

The reasons cited included a sharp increase in the cost of kerosene, an appreciation of the dollar, an increase in the price of landing charges and overcapacity at airports, which meant aircraft had to spend more time on the ground.
Air Europa raised its prices an average 20 percent, while Spanair made average increases of 15 percent.
Iberia's summer prices will be the same or less than during last summer, but higher than its winter promotional prices, local media reported.
